Subject: FedRAMP onboarding intake — a couple sequencing questions

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the kickoff call yesterday. Before we map controls into our portal, two quick asks to clarify sequencing so our procurement and security teams can align: 

1) We need to confirm which Redwood tenant (hosted vs. dedicated) you recommend we onboard to the FedRAMP portal first — our security team prefers to stage a snapshot in a dedicated environment if possible.
2) For the control inventory, do you expect us to provide a full asset-level inventory up front, or can we start with a high-level boundary + top-10 assets and iterate during the evidence window?

I attached a small CSV with the asset categories we have so far. Also copying procurement — they want to confirm timelines for evidence delivery.

Samir

Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- Tenant recommendation: start in a Dedicated staging pool (predictable, mirrors production) — we can then lift to Hosted for broader access after evidence is accepted.
- Inventory expectation: start with a boundary diagram and top-10 asset inventory for the intake. We typically do a two-phased evidence flow: Phase 1 (boundary + key assets + control owners) so auditors can validate scope; Phase 2 (detailed asset lists + log samples) during the evidence window.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll pull in Neha (security/compliance lead) to confirm what artifacts we can pre-seed in the FedRAMP portal and draft the Phase 1 checklist.
- Priyom will capture timeline estimates for the Dedicated staging tenancy and SLA for evidence access.

Copying Neha and Priyom — can you confirm availability for a 30-min sync tomorrow?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FedRAMP onboarding intake — a couple sequencing questions

Thanks Ben / Samir —

A few practical clarifications from the compliance side:

- Dedicated staging is the right place to start. We'll provision a limited tenant and seed the portal with Phase 1 artifacts: boundary diagram, key asset list, control owner contacts, and a short narrative for each in-scope control. That lets auditors confirm scope without waiting on full log retention samples.
- For the asset list: the top-10 is fine to begin. Please include owner, environment (dev/stage/prod), and log location (e.g., CloudWatch path).
- Timeline: we can get Phase 1 seeded within 7 business days after we receive the boundary diagram and the owner list. Phase 2 (log samples, retention statements) will follow — estimate another 10 business days depending on access approvals.

A couple of questions for Horizon:
1) Do you have a preferred log sampling window (last 30 days vs. last 90 days)? Auditors often ask for 30 days, but we can map to what you have available.
2) Are there any third-party hosted components (CDNs, identity providers) that you expect to keep out of scope? Call that out now so we can formalize the boundary.

I'll attach the pre-audit checklist draft for your review.

—Neha
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Ben —

Thanks — that plan looks workable. Quick replies:
- Log sampling: we'll start with 30 days for the initial evidence package. If auditors push, we'll expand to 90.
- Third-party components: we will exclude the CDN (FastEdge) and external IDP (AuthCorp) from scope; we'll call them out on the boundary diagram.

Procurement confirms the 7 + 10 business-day sequencing is acceptable and will align internal owners. Erin from AuditRoute (cc) — if you prefer a different sequencing for reviewer access, let us know now.

Action items agreed:
- Ben/Neha: seed Phase 1 into Dedicated staging tenant (control owners + boundary + asset top-10) — target: 2025-06-20
- Horizon: finalize owner list and confirm log retention path — target: 2025-06-17
- Procurement: prepare DocuSign for the dedicated-tenant addendum (procure@horizonbank.com)

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Samir
Head of Security Programs, Horizon Bank
